sources.title: WIPO — From a Mountain Walk to 2,100 Patents: The Velcro IP Story

youtube.title: Velcro Invention: How a Weed Stuck on a Dog Started It
youtube.description:
The Velcro invention began with a weed stuck on a dog. Swiss engineer George de Mestral came home from a walk in the Swiss mountains with his dog covered in burdock burrs, and instead of just pulling them off, he put one under a microscope.

He saw hundreds of tiny hooks that grabbed every loop of fur and thread. So he copied nature: hooks on one strip, loops on the other. Cotton wore out fast, nylon held, it took him years, and he named his hook-and-loop fastener Velcro, from the French velours (velvet) and crochet (hook). And no, NASA did not invent it; astronauts only made it famous.

Subscribe to Stickstory for a true story like this every day. What everyday thing do you think was copied from nature? Tell me in the comments!

scenes.text: A weed on a dog invented this.
scenes.visual: Hook frame in an Alpine meadow under snowy peaks: the fez host stands big in shock (hands up, round 'O' mouth, shock ticks); in his left hand a giant spiky burr whose spikes end in tiny hooks, from his right hand hangs a red hook strip with a blue loop strip half peeled off it; a bold red dashed arrow swings under his arms from the burr to the strap; a sitting dog covered in burrs on the left.

scenes.text: George de Mestral came home from a walk in the Swiss mountains.
scenes.visual: Wide shot of the Swiss mountains: snowy peaks, a wooden chalet with a smoking chimney on the right; George de Mestral (hatless, red sweater) stands at the door; his dog runs in from the left past two burdock plants, picks up burrs at each one and sits in front of him; George's hand goes to his head; red card 'SWITZERLAND', hand label 'George de Mestral'.

scenes.text: His dog was covered in burrs.
scenes.visual: Close-up of the sitting dog with worried brows: one spiky burr after another pops onto its coat, back and head; a burdock plant with burr heads stands on the right, grass in front.

scenes.text: Most of us pull them off.
scenes.visual: The fez host stands in the meadow, annoyed, five big burrs stuck on his legs; from 'pull' they fly off one by one in high arcs; burdock plants on both sides.

scenes.text: Under a microscope, George saw tiny hooks,
scenes.visual: Indoors at a wooden desk under a hanging lamp: George sits and leans into a microscope with a tiny burr on its slide; a big magnified bubble opens above right, joined to the eyepiece by dashed lines, showing the burr turning, every spike ending in a hook; a red ring circles one hook; red box 'TINY HOOKS'.

Full-frame view through the eyepiece (dark ring round a bright circle): thick ink hooks hang from the burr's skin at the top; loops rise from fur at the bottom; on 'grabbing' the hooks drop and catch each loop, then tug; labels 'HOOKS' and 'LOOPS'.

scenes.text: He copied it: hooks on one strip, loops on another. It took years.
scenes.visual: A big workbench top fills the frame (y 580–1190): a burr lies at the top between serif cards 'HOOKS' and 'LOOPS'; a tall white strip covered in big hooks and a tall blue strip covered in loops slide in on their words; on 'another' the strips press together and pull apart again with red rip marks.

Two test rigs hang from a wooden beam, each a pair of strips holding an iron weight: on 'Cotton' the left pair frays and its weight drops onto the bench, a big red X stamps over it, label 'COTTON'; on 'Nylon' the blue right pair keeps swinging with its weight and a green tick appears, label 'NYLON'.

scenes.text: The name Velcro? Velvet and hook, in French.
scenes.visual: A big cork pinboard fills the wall: 'VELCRO' pops in a red box at the top; on 'Velvet' an arrow runs from VEL down to a pinned card 'VELOURS' with a red hand note 'velvet', on 'hook' an arrow from CRO to 'CROCHET' with 'hook'; a burr on the desk below.

scenes.text: That rip on your shoes? A Swiss weed.
scenes.visual: A child's sneaker on a wooden floor: on 'rip' its two red hook-and-loop straps peel up with red rip marks and a big red 'RIIIP!' top left; on 'weed' a big spiky burr pops in right above the straps and a bold red arrow points from it to the strap's hooks.

scenes.text: Subscribe for a true story every day.
scenes.visual: Back in the Alpine meadow: the fez host stands big on the left and waves, then points at the viewer; his dog sits on the right wagging its tail with one burr on its back; a burdock plant behind, snowy peaks far away.
